sentences.text: The bird showed osteosclerosis, a bone thickening that is often associated with diving adaptations.
Its high metabolic rate would have helped it endure the cold, high-latitude conditions of ancient Antarctica.
Vegavis notopothousa was described by Irazoqui and colleagues.
The type locality is the López de Bertodano Formation in Antarctica.
The species was formally named in 2026.
Its specific epithet combines Greek words meaning 'south' and 'longing', alluding to the fossil's Southern Hemisphere origin and its present curation in the Northern Hemisphere.
Vegavis notopothousa is placed within the neornithine clade, a group of modern birds.
It belongs to the order Anseriformes, the lineage that includes ducks, geese and swans.
The species lived during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, about 69.2 million years ago.
The broader genus Vegavis existed between 72.2 and 66 million years ago, spanning most of the Maastrichtian.
